detailed_analysis: The pattern is fit with 30 split pseudo-Voigt reflections on a SNIP background over 4.5-45 deg. Global R2 = 0.9999994 is inflated by background channels; the diagnostic metric peak_region_r2 = 0.9993 passes cleanly, so peak positions and integrated intensities are reliable. Two dominant reflections at 2theta = 11.04 and 22.20 deg (amplitudes ~1.1e6 each) plus strong features near 17-21 and 26-36 deg define the phase's characteristic fingerprint. Refined FWHMs cluster around 0.2-0.5 deg, placing most reflections in the typical microcrystalline regime (30-100 nm) with several dipping into the nanocrystalline regime (10-30 nm). Per-peak Scherrer sizes range from ~17 to ~43 nm across the well-behaved peaks (mean ~26 nm), a spread >2.5x that flags anisotropic (hkl-dependent) broadening; the isotropic Scherrer mean is therefore an oversimplification and the RANGE should be quoted, not a single number. Two of the fitted 'peaks' (peak_1 FWHM=1.37 deg, peak_3 FWHM=2.0 deg, both eta~0.99) are broad, Lorentzian-dominated features near the low-angle edge that are almost certainly residual background/amorphous contributions absorbed by the peak model rather than genuine crystallite reflections; their Scherrer 'sizes' of 3-6 nm should be discarded. The Williamson-Hall analysis is invalid: R2 = 0.10 with a NEGATIVE slope (implied strain -0.0055), which the domain rules classify as unphysical (bad-background/anisotropy/misassignment signature). Per mandate, the size+strain decomposition is NOT reported; only per-peak Scherrer sizes are. Residuals reach up to 34x noise at the apex of the sharpest peaks (22.2, 11) with a symmetric up-down-up oscillation and a coherent multi-sigma band across the 18.6/19.2/20.2/20.9 cluster; per domain validation these are the irreducible split-PV profile limit and mild overlap at the resolution boundary of the strongest reflections, not unmodelled reflections (no isolated new-peak spikes), so the fit is correctly accepted. Since this is frame 1 of a variable-temperature dehydration series, these positions/widths establish the baseline hydrated-phase fingerprint against which peak shifts (lattice contraction), intensity changes, and any phase transition in later frames should be tracked.

scientific_claims.claim: The hydrated phase at 28.7 C is microcrystalline with anisotropic broadening: per-peak Scherrer coherent domain sizes span ~17-43 nm (mean ~26 nm, ~+/-15% instrumental accuracy) across the well-fit reflections, with no reliable microstrain (Williamson-Hall R2 = 0.10, negative slope => decomposition not applicable).
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Establishes the crystallite-size baseline and fingerprint of the starting (frame-1) phase in an in-situ dehydration series, and shows broadening is hkl-dependent (anisotropic domain shape) rather than strain-driven; this is the reference state for detecting lattice contraction, intensity redistribution, or a dehydration-induced phase transition in subsequent frames.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone observed anisotropic, hkl-dependent crystallite-size broadening (17-43 nm domains) with negligible microstrain in the starting hydrated phase of this material by in-situ synchrotron powder XRD prior to dehydration?

model_type: Sum of split pseudo-Voigt peaks (auto-detect prominence_frac=0.01, min_distance=0.10, plus seeded shoulders at 26.25 and 29.3) on SNIP background; fit_range=(4.5,45.0) to exclude giant ~3.3 deg low-angle feature

verification_iterations.model: Sum of split (asymmetric) pseudo-Voigt peaks (one per detected Bragg reflection) on a SNIP background. Pseudo-Voigt mixing eta free per peak in [0,1]. Auto-detect determines the peak count (expect ~10–15 reflections across the fitted range); no hardcoded centers so the recipe generalizes across the in-situ series frames.

issues.problem: The main peak apex/wings are under-resolved: the residual shows a clear symmetric oscillation (up-down-up, 2 sign-changes) at 65σ centered on the strong peak.
Under-resolved shoulder on the high-angle side of the ~26.0 peak — the fit misses a clear data maximum/shoulder near 26.2–26.3.
Under-resolved shoulder on the low-angle side of the 29.79 peak — the fit does not cover the data shoulder near 29.3.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Re-run fit_pattern with prominence_frac≈0.01 and add/seed components near x≈26.25 and x≈29.3; verify the split-pseudo-Voigt shape for the 22.2 peak captures its apex asymmetry.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of split (asymmetric) pseudo-Voigt peaks (one per detected Bragg reflection) on a SNIP background. Pseudo-Voigt mixing eta free per peak in [0,1]; split shape allows independent left/right FWHM to capture apex/wing asymmetry. Peak count is set by auto-detection (expect ~12–17 reflections across the fitted range now that low-intensity shoulders are resolved), with no hardcoded centers so the recipe generalizes across the in-situ VT series. Explicit seeded components are added near x≈26.25 (high-angle shoulder of the 25.97 peak) and x≈29.3 (low-angle shoulder of the 29.79 peak) to represent genuine but weak reflections previously merged into their neighbors. Model itself is LOCKED — only detection sensitivity and per-peak shape freedom are adjusted.
